change: temporal context: 7.5 min centred triangular-weighted rolling average plus 2 min trailing average, per feature, within night
conclusion: Temporal context improves both tasks by roughly +0.07 kappa, replicating across two different label sets, which is what makes it credible rather than a lucky split. It is not sufficient: 9 of 16 and 7 of 16 subjects show skill, and the worst subject is barely above chance. Offline only -- the centred window reads future epochs.

negative_result.change: frequency-domain HRV (LF, HF, LF/HF, normalised HF) over a 5-minute centred window, added on top of temporal context
negative_result.outcome: worse on both tasks: four-class kappa +0.280 -> +0.233 and 9 -> 7 subjects with skill; sleep/wake +0.287 -> +0.280 and 7 -> 6. Not shipped: load_epochs(with_frequency=False) is the default.
candidate_explanations_untested: 48 features against 8622 samples gives more room to overfit than 36
windows that cannot support an estimate emit 0.0, making 'not estimable' indistinguishable from 'no power' to the model
epochs near the start and end of a record have truncated windows and so produce disproportionately many of those zeros

followup.hypothesis: the regression was feature count, not the features -- so keep only normalised_hf, which is bounded and comparable across subjects
followup.outcome: refuted. One feature performs the same as four and neither beats context alone. Frequency-domain HRV over 5-minute windows adds no signal beyond what the smoothed time-domain features already carry, on this dataset.
followup.remaining: The zero-fill and truncated-edge explanations are now also unlikely, since a single bounded feature would be far less affected by both and still did not help.
